key_insight: Exact boundary and initial constraints enable PINNs to identify the shear piezoelectric coefficient e15 accurately from sparse, noisy simulated wavefields without tuning boundary or initial-condition penalty weights.
engineering_relevance: The approach could support non-destructive characterization of shear-mode coupling in PMUTs and SAW devices, potentially replacing dedicated destructive resonance tests.
method: Embed spatial distance functions and temporal multipliers into network outputs to enforce clamped, grounded boundaries and a resting initial state exactly.
Train using coupled electro-elastodynamic equations and observation misfit, with non-dimensional scaling to balance governing coefficients.
Use a quadratic temporal multiplier to reduce early-time electrostatic residuals.
evidence_signal: On simulated plane-strain PZT-5H data, constrained variants achieved 0.15–0.51% mean e15 error in a six-way comparison; the full formulation achieved 1.19% on finite-element data at 30 dB noise.
watch_item: Validation is limited to simulated data; experimental robustness and construction of exact constraint functions for complex device geometries remain untested.
paper_title: Identifying the Shear Piezoelectric Coefficient using Physics-Informed Neural Networks under Exact Boundary and Initial Constraints
